neighbours.label: clause-final punctuation after a claim that the writer is about to qualify or rebut
fire: Some readers will think I exaggerated the danger, but if anything I played it down.
They were sure they had the best team in the league. Someone must have cheated them.
Surely there are plenty of bees around! After all, you see them every summer.
Why worry about the disease when it was not even here? That was the common view.
Critics claim the plan is far too costly, yet it would save money within a decade.
Many assume the river is too cold for fish, but trout thrive in it.
People say the old bridge is perfectly safe. The engineers disagree.
You might think the desert is empty of life, but it is full of insects.
quiet: I described the danger carefully in the second chapter of the report.
They had a strong team in the league and won most of their games.
Bees visit the garden every summer and pollinate the apple trees.
The disease arrived in the region during the dry season.
The plan costs a lot and will be paid for over a decade.
The river is cold and fast and flows north to the sea.
The old bridge was built in 1902 from local stone.
The desert stretches for hundreds of miles to the south.
